new_points.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
new_points.content: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight. Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than with conventional methods. The technology has already uncovered a previously hidden planet in existing telescope data and could reveal many more.

new_points.title: A mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure may be the wreckage of colliding worlds

The discovery challenges previous assumptions about the structure and offers new clues about the violent birth of planetary systems.

new_points.title: Comets may have destroyed life's ingredients instead of delivering them to Earth
new_points.content: A century-old theory about the origins of life on Earth may be wrong. New research from the University of Cambridge suggests that comets traveled too fast and struck at unfavorable angles for the fragile molecules needed for life to survive, making successful delivery extraordinarily unlikely. Surprisingly, Mars may have had a better chance of receiving these cosmic ingredients, although even there the odds were slim. The findings point toward asteroids or chemical processes on Earth as more plausible sources of life's building blocks.

new_points.title: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue
new_points.content: Scientists have discovered a remarkably preserved 450-million-year-old fossil containing soft tissues from an ancient starfish relative, revealing unexpected details about marine life more than 200 million years before dinosaurs existed. Found in a museum collection, the extraordinarily rare specimen offers new clues about how Earth's earliest reef animals fed, survived, and evolved.
